name: Roku, Inc.

profile.description: Roku operates a TV streaming platform made up of the Roku operating system licensed to TV makers, Roku-branded TVs and players, The Roku Channel, and advertising and subscription businesses. Founded in 2002 by CEO Anthony Wood and headquartered in San Jose, it now reports Advertising and Subscriptions as separate segments. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.35B (+22% YoY), with Platform revenue of $1.22B (+25%). Q3 2026 results are scheduled after the close on November 2, 2026 [1][2][6].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Over five years Roku shifted from a device maker to a platform business. Platform revenue reached $1.22B of $1.35B total in Q2 2026, and the company has added Roku-made TVs, a separate Subscriptions segment and the Howdy streaming service [1][2][10]. Platform growth accelerated from 17% in Q3 2025 to 28% in Q1 2026 [2][13]. AI Deployment (1/2): Wood has described AI originals helping Howdy become a mainstream service within 5-10 years, but no shipping AI product revenue or quantified AI savings were found [10]. Market Share (1/2): Platform revenue growth of 25% shows share momentum in TV advertising, but no audited share data was found in research [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management expects sustained double-digit Platform growth and is building subscription offerings, without named launch dates or revenue targets [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): TTM R&D runs at 14.1% of revenue, well above media and entertainment peers [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Roku's founding thesis that TV would move to streaming has guided the company since 2002, but its public mission reads as a platform-strategy statement rather than a distinctive purpose beyond the business [7][8]. Community Impact (0/2): Searches found no foundation, quantified giving or community programs. The most visible stakeholder issue was consumer backlash over new mandatory dispute-resolution terms that blocked device use until users accepted them [12]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found; filings warn that growth could erode the company's entrepreneurial culture [7]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP records no open-market insider purchases in 2026 against more than 140 sales across Q1-Q4 2026 [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically (Growth sleeve): D/E of 16.8% (1.00), ROE of 13.2% (0.88, 2x), YoY revenue growth of 21.9% in Q2 2026 (1.00), 5-year revenue CAGR of 21.6% from FY2020-FY2025 (1.00, 2x), forward P/E of 39.4 (0.52), TTM net margin of 6.8% (0.34) and forward PEG of 0.08 per FMP (1.00, 2x). Weighted sum is 8.61/10, which rounds to 9 [3][4]. Forward P/E is derived from the $155.12 price and FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.94. TTM free cash flow of about $826M and net cash on the balance sheet support the score. Daily dollar volume of about $400M easily clears the liquidity floor [3].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Roku controls the TV operating system and home screen used by its installed base. Generative AI is more likely to multiply the content and ads flowing through that gatekeeper position than to replace it, and AI-driven ad targeting strengthens platform monetization [1]. The risk is that AI assistants built into rival TV operating systems from large tech platforms reshape discovery and erode the home-screen advantage, and research found no analyst work showing Roku is insulated [7]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Roku has discussed AI-generated originals for Howdy and AI in its products, but reports no quantifiable AI revenue [10].

infinite_game.summary: Under founder Anthony Wood, Roku has spent two decades on a single thesis, that all TV will be streamed, and reinvented itself from a hardware company into a licensing and advertising platform to pursue it. That consistency and adaptability are infinite-game traits. A finite, rival-beating competitive posture, consumer-hostile policy moves and no visible insider conviction keep it in the MIXED range.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Wood's long-held vision that TV will move to streaming has outlasted the Netflix player project, the 2017 IPO and the 2022-2023 loss cycle, and it still drives strategy [7][8]. It is a vision of how an industry evolves more than a service-oriented cause that benefits others, which keeps it below a 3.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): A longtime colleague describes Wood as a risk-taker who encourages employees to take risks too, and filings call culture a key retention tool [7][9]. The same filings flag heavy dependence on Wood, the lack of long-term employment agreements and the risk of losing the entrepreneurial culture as the company grows, so trust is adequate rather than exceptional [7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Wood is profiled as a mild-mannered executive who has beaten larger rivals, and Roku's positioning against much bigger technology platforms is framed as a contest to win rather than one to learn from [8]. Research found no management commentary acknowledging competitors' strengths as a source of improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Roku began by building a streaming player for Netflix, then moved from selling hardware to licensing its operating system to TV makers and earning most of its revenue from advertising and subscriptions. Platform revenue was $1.22B of $1.35B in Q2 2026 [1][8]. It has kept extending that model with Roku-made TVs and subscription services like Howdy, a reinvention driven by the streaming thesis rather than desperation [2][10].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Roku kept investing heavily in R&D ($878M in FY2023) and platform growth through net losses of $498M in FY2022 and $710M in FY2023, choosing scale over near-term profit [3]. The mandatory dispute-terms episode suggests a willingness to put corporate protection ahead of customer goodwill, so the record is mixed [12].

investment_thesis: Roku has reached sustained profitability on top of accelerating growth. Q2 2026 revenue rose 22% to $1.35B, Platform revenue rose 25% to $1.22B, and TTM net income reached about $355M after losses of $710M in FY2023 [1][3]. Platform growth accelerated from 17% in Q3 2025 to 25-28% in the first half of 2026, and management expects double-digit Platform growth to continue [1][2][13]. TTM free cash flow of about $826M, D/E of 16.8% and net cash give the company room to keep investing. Consensus EPS climbs from $3.94 in FY2027 to $6.69 in FY2029, and Roku's control of the TV home screen makes it a toll collector on the shift of TV advertising to streaming [4].
thesis_continued: Valuation is demanding: 64.6x trailing earnings and about 39x FY2027 consensus EPS, after a rally toward the top of the 52-week range ($78.53-$160.22). Q3 2026 results tonight (November 2) are an immediate volatility event [3][6]. Net margin is only 6.8%, so earnings remain highly sensitive to ad-market cycles. Larger platforms with their own TV operating systems and AI assistants could pressure Roku's home-screen economics [7]. Governance and culture concentrate on founder Anthony Wood with no key-person insurance, insiders are persistent net sellers, and consumer backlash over forced arbitration terms points to brand-trust risk [5][7][12].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results on November 2, 2026, the test of whether Platform revenue can hold 20%+ growth against the 17% Q3 2025 comparison
Scaling the newly separated Subscriptions segment, including Howdy, to diversify beyond advertising
Operating leverage as revenue grows faster than costs, with consensus EPS rising from $3.94 (FY2027) to $6.69 (FY2029)
key_risks: Competitors' TV operating systems with AI assistants capturing content discovery and ad inventory from Roku's home screen
Cyclical ad-market exposure on a thin 6.8% net margin and a 39x forward multiple, where a growth slowdown would compress both earnings and valuation
Key-person dependence on founder-CEO Anthony Wood, with no key-person insurance or long-term employment agreements for executives
